author: Vitor
notes: The map keeps the score per level, although a stack could have been used.
aiExplanation: This function computes the **score of a balanced parentheses string**, where `()` is worth **1**, two side-by-side groups `AB` add up (`A + B`), and a group wrapped in another pair `(A)` is worth **double** (`2 * A`). It walks the string once while tracking the current nesting `depth` and keeps a `Map` from each depth to the running score accumulated at that level, starting with depth `0` at score `0`. Every time it sees an opening `(` it goes one level deeper and resets that level's score to `0`, since a fresh group is starting. When it sees a closing `)` it steps back up one level and decides what that just-closed group is worth: if the previous character was `(`, the group was an empty `()` and contributes **1**; otherwise it contained nested content, so it contributes **twice** the score that was collected at the deeper level (`map.get(depth + 1)`). That value is then **added** to the score of the level it just returned to, which naturally handles sibling groups being summed. Once the loop finishes, everything has bubbled up to depth `0`, so `map.get(0)` is the final answer, all in **O(n)** time.
